title: Beneath the Double Coat — The Secret in the Snow
productionNotes:
Prestige daytime soap opera performed by photorealistic Bernese Mountain Dogs. Every character, including veterinarian and groundskeeper, is a dog. Absolute dramatic sincerity; humor comes from canine instincts interrupting melodrama. Real quadrupedal anatomy, paws and weight. Restrained speaking muzzle animation, expressive ears and posture; no human hands or upright bodies. Objects are moved with noses, mouths and paws.
Alpenrose Estate: Alpine mansion, snow outside, dark carved wood, Persian rugs, warm lamps and marble floors. Hard cuts for new angles or locations; continuous movement within connected shots. No automatic fades. Preserve identities, collar colors, voices and room geography across cuts. Only the named characters appear.
HEIDI: elderly female, silver muzzle, narrow blaze, burgundy collar; low imperious voice. SEBASTIAN, initially called BRUNO: large male, symmetrical rust eyebrows, broad white chest, immaculate coat, navy collar, no ear scar; smooth defensive voice. REAL BRUNO: nearly identical male, weathered coat, faded brown collar, four-stitch scar on LEFT ear; warm gravelly voice. SADIE: slender blaze, emerald collar; precise, controlled female voice. MAPLE: rounded rust eyebrows, teal collar and stethoscope; clipped professional female voice. OTTO: stocky shaggy male, ochre collar; earnest breathless voice. PENNY: small fluffy puppy, lavender collar, innocent voice. MYSTERY DOG: massive Bernese with silver tag, face obscured.
Use the scripted dialogue exactly, with no narrator except the labeled flashback voiceover. Original mournful piano, trembling strings and restrained organ, always below speech. Room tone from first frame, paw steps and collar jingles. Dramatic stings followed by silence for comic reactions. No laugh track. Readable title and evidence inserts will require editorial overlays if generation cannot reproduce their text.
This is a condensed adaptation of the supplied episode. Keep its reveals, not the exact runtime of the full screenplay. Explicit ages and elapsed years are omitted pending a chronology decision. References and voice performances must be approved before full production.
reviewNotes: This is the condensed adaptation, not a verbatim production of the full original screenplay. Review the pacing and omitted lines before production.
Chronology needs a decision: the original lists Bruno as five, an eight-year impersonation, and a father dead for twelve years. This adaptation omits explicit ages and elapsed years.
Approve character references and voice performances before producing the full cast. Descriptions alone do not guarantee identity or voice consistency across cuts.
Dialogue and sound are preserved in the script, but the current generation compiler still suppresses spoken dialogue and does not forward planned sound. Resolve this before generating these shots.
Readable evidence and titles (thermostat, photograph, bowl) need editorial overlays if generated text is inaccurate.
No video, narration, music or sound effects have been generated. This import only creates a reviewable plan and timeline.

shots.title: Muddy footprints
shots.dialogue: HEIDI (offscreen): No... it cannot be.
shots.visual: Dawn aerial of snowy Alpenrose Estate, then a low view of muddy paw prints on immaculate front steps. No dogs visible.
shots.audio: Cold wind, distant bark, a low piano note.

shots.title: The discovery
shots.dialogue: HEIDI: After all these years... You are alive.
shots.visual: Grooming room. Heidi sniffs black fur beside a silver undercoat rake on a low platform. Her ears rise.
shots.audio: Low original soap-opera score beneath dialogue; continuous room ambience.

shots.title: Locked in
shots.dialogue: HEIDI: Who is there?
shots.visual: A shadow crosses the hall. Heidi turns. Door closes; she rushes to paw it.
shots.audio: Door latch clicks. Ventilation hum abruptly stops.

shots.title: The thermostat
shots.dialogue: HEIDI: You would not.
shots.visual: Close insert of digital thermostat rising from 72°F to 73°F; cut to Heidi staring, horrified.
shots.audio: Silence where the vent had been. Rising strings.

shots.title: You monster
shots.dialogue: HEIDI: YOU MONSTER!
shots.visual: Thermostat reaches 74°F. Heidi throws her front paws against the door. End black.
shots.audio: Paw impacts, dramatic sting, abrupt silence.

shots.title: Title
shots.visual: Black title card: BENEATH THE DOUBLE COAT. Macro insert of a strand of drool falling in slow motion.
shots.audio: One mournful piano note.

shots.title: Breakfast accusation
shots.dialogue:
SADIE: You came home at two.
BRUNO: I went for a walk.
SADIE: For six hours?
shots.visual: Breakfast room. Household Bruno has front paws on a chair, back paws on floor. Sadie opposite; final cheddar cube between them.
shots.audio: Low original soap-opera score beneath dialogue; continuous room ambience.

shots.title: Parmesan
shots.dialogue:
SADIE: Parmesan.
BRUNO: Sadie—
SADIE: There is no Parmesan in this house.
shots.visual: Sadie sniffs Bruno’s muzzle. His eyes flick toward the cheddar. Her ears freeze.
shots.audio: Low original soap-opera score beneath dialogue; continuous room ambience.

shots.title: Rosemary
shots.dialogue:
SADIE: And rosemary. You saw Bella.
BRUNO: Nothing happened.
shots.visual: Sadie circles Bruno and sniffs again. His ears twitch involuntarily.
shots.audio: Low original soap-opera score beneath dialogue; continuous room ambience.

shots.title: Imported cheese
shots.dialogue:
SADIE: Then why do you smell like imported cheese?
OTTO: It is Heidi.
shots.visual: Close on Sadie, then Bruno trying to look innocent. Otto bursts through doorway.
shots.audio: Low original soap-opera score beneath dialogue; continuous room ambience.

shots.title: Air conditioning
shots.dialogue: OTTO: Someone locked her in the grooming room. And turned off the air conditioning.
shots.visual: Otto breathless in doorway. Sadie and Bruno turn toward him.
shots.audio: Low original soap-opera score beneath dialogue; continuous room ambience.

shots.title: A dead dog
shots.dialogue:
SADIE: Bruno?
BRUNO: That fur belongs to a dead dog.
shots.visual: Otto deposits folded cloth with black fur on a low table. Bruno sniffs, then recoils.
shots.audio: Dramatic sting; hard cut to black.

shots.title: Cooling room
shots.dialogue:
BRUNO: Grandmother.
HEIDI: You always were clingy.
MAPLE: You need rest.
shots.visual: Heidi on cool marble with ice packs and three fans. Maple examines her; Bruno presses close.
shots.audio: Fans roar softly beneath clear dialogue.

shots.title: The brother
shots.dialogue:
HEIDI: You know whose fur it was. Your brother’s.
BRUNO: You should rest.
shots.visual: Heidi fixes Bruno with a penetrating look.
shots.audio: Low original soap-opera score beneath dialogue; continuous room ambience.

shots.title: Sebastian
shots.dialogue:
SADIE: You have a brother?
BRUNO: Had.
HEIDI: Apparently not. Sebastian.
shots.visual: Sadie appears in doorway. Bruno avoids her gaze. Heidi stays still.
shots.audio: Low original soap-opera score beneath dialogue; continuous room ambience.

shots.title: Maple reacts
shots.dialogue:
HEIDI: You know that name.
MAPLE: I have another appointment.
shots.visual: Maple’s stethoscope slips and clatters. Everyone turns toward her.
shots.audio: Metal clatter, silence, then restrained tension.

shots.title: Seasonal allergies
shots.dialogue:
SADIE: With who?
MAPLE: A Labradoodle with seasonal allergies.
HEIDI: Follow her.
shots.visual: Maple edges toward door, Sadie watches; Heidi follows Maple with her eyes.
shots.audio: Low original soap-opera score beneath dialogue; continuous room ambience.

shots.title: Poor stealth
shots.visual: Snowy garden. Sadie barely fits behind hedge while tailing Maple. Branch snaps; squirrel distracts Maple.
shots.audio: Branch snap, paw steps, playful low strings.

shots.title: Secret knock
shots.visual: Maple taps toolshed door three times, twice, then scratches. She slips inside; Sadie approaches window.
shots.audio: Distinct coded taps and scratch, door creak.

shots.title: Done running
shots.dialogue:
MAPLE: Heidi found the fur. You have to leave.
STRANGER: I am done running.
shots.visual: Inside shed. Maple faces a large Bernese whose back is turned.
shots.audio: Low original soap-opera score beneath dialogue; continuous room ambience.

shots.title: Not alone
shots.dialogue: MAPLE: Bruno believes you are dead.
shots.visual: Through window, Sadie watches. Stranger’s ears perk. She ducks and sneezes explosively.
shots.audio: Muted dialogue through glass, enormous sneeze.

shots.title: I am Bruno
shots.dialogue:
SADIE: Sebastian?
STRANGER: No.
SADIE: Who are you?
STRANGER: I am Bruno.
shots.visual: Shed door opens. Stranger resembles Bruno but scar remains hidden by angle. Sadie looks up.
shots.audio: Slow rising strings, cut to black.

script.title: Part Two — The Wrong Dog
script.sourceTranscript:
HEIDI: Sit.

HEIDI: Interesting. Come here.
BRUNO: Why?
HEIDI: Because no one tells me no anymore.

HEIDI: Where is the scar?
BRUNO: What scar?

HEIDI: The dishwasher. Beef gravy. Four stitches.
BRUNO: Scars fade.
HEIDI: Not that one.

HEIDI: Who are you?
BRUNO: You should have stayed in the grooming room.

PENNY: Dad?
BRUNO: Penny.

PENNY: Why did you lock Great-Grandma in the hot room? I found this under your bed.

REAL BRUNO: The dishwasher. Beef gravy.
SADIE: Then who have I been married to?

MAPLE: Sebastian.
SADIE: You said he was dead.
REAL BRUNO: There was no kennel fire.

SADIE: Then what happened?
REAL BRUNO: A dryer.

REAL BRUNO (voiceover): He loved it. I hated it.

REAL BRUNO (voiceover): I ran. He took my collar.

SADIE: A collar does not make someone another dog. What about their microchips?

MAPLE: There was a clerical error.
SADIE: You switched the dogs?
MAPLE: I was an intern.

SADIE: YOU SWITCHED THE DOGS?
MAPLE: I PANICKED!

REAL BRUNO: Sebastian knew. He never corrected them.
SADIE: He stole your life.

SADIE: He stole mine too.
MAPLE: There is something else.

MAPLE: Penny is not Sebastian’s daughter.
SADIE: What are you saying?

SADIE: No.

SADIE: Penny!

script.title: Part Three — Some Secrets Shed Forever
script.sourceTranscript:
HEIDI: You always were jealous.
SEBASTIAN: You loved him more.

SEBASTIAN: I did not mean to do that.

HEIDI: You cried over a houseplant.
SEBASTIAN: It was a very nice houseplant.

HEIDI: You could have come home as yourself.
SADIE: Instead, you came home as my husband.

REAL BRUNO: Hello, brother.
PENNY: Why are there two Dads?

SEBASTIAN: I was going to tell them. After the holidays.
SADIE: WHICH HOLIDAYS?
SEBASTIAN: I had not decided!

BOTH BROTHERS: Rotisserie chicken.
SADIE: Are you serious?

SADIE: Who is that?
HEIDI: That is impossible.

PENNY: But there are three puppies.
HEIDI: There were only two.

SEBASTIAN: That is yours.
REAL BRUNO: No.

HEIDI: I know that bark.
REAL BRUNO: Whose is it?

HEIDI: Your father’s.
REAL BRUNO: My father is dead.

HEIDI: I know. I buried him.

SADIE: One of you is Penny’s father.

HEIDI: The collar was here!
MAPLE: These are not his hips.

OTTO: Then whose hips are they?
PENNY: I can explain.

SADIE (offscreen): He is inside the house.

MYSTERY DOG: Ask Heidi why there is one grave... but two headstones.
